correctness.rationale: Testing invariant measures against arbitrary antiderivatives of x gives E[y|x]=0, and testing against arbitrary antiderivatives of z gives E[x^2|z]=alpha z. Conditional orthogonality yields both Cov(x^2,z)=alpha Var(z) and Var(x^2)-alpha^2 Var(z)=E[dot z^2]. Stationarity of xy, together with E[xy]=0 and the z-fiber law, gives Var(y)=alpha E[z(z-1)]. The conditional law forces z>=0 on support. If Var(y)=0, invariance of the compact support forces every complete bounded trajectory there to be one of O or P_±; hence any non-equilibrium-supported measure has positive E[z(z-1)] and therefore positive mass on z>1. Variation of constants gives the exact exponential-memory formula for every bounded complete trajectory. The packaged checker independently verifies all algebraic identities used in these reductions.

value.rationale: The height variable z is the quadratic-amplitude filter that distinguishes the Shimizu–Morioka normal form from a generic three-dimensional oscillator, and z=1 is the common height of its two nonzero equilibria. The accepted theorem turns that architecture into an exact stationary law: every height fiber has mean squared amplitude alpha z, while every non-equilibrium recurrent statistical state must overshoot the outer-equilibrium height. The variance and covariance identities quantify how closely x^2 tracks the filtered height through the mean-square z-speed. These facts give parameter-exact diagnostics for periodic and chaotic invariant measures and complement, rather than duplicate, the established bifurcation and Lorenz-attractor theory.
